aspects.says: A static factory picks the class of its result from its input, as EnumSet picks RegularEnumSet or JumboEnumSet from the enum's size, so the class can change without any caller changing.
basis: section:A Static Factory Picks the Class From Its Input, So the Class Can Change Without Callers Noticing

aspects.says: The GoF factory method is an overridable creation method that base-class code calls, so one override changes the product for every caller, and each overload callers reach must be overridden.
basis: section:The GoF Factory Method Is a Creation Hook That Base-Class Code Calls and a Subclass Overrides

aspects.says: A static factory can hand back an object it already made where new must allocate; sharing is safe only for immutable objects, and a cache keyed by caller input must stay bounded.
basis: section:new Always Allocates; a Static Factory Can Hand Back an Object It Already Made

aspects.says: A factory passed to the creator, such as ThreadPoolExecutor's ThreadFactory, works with any creator that accepts it without a subclass, but sees only what the creator hands it.
basis: section:Each Product Costs a Subclass, and the Hook Reaches Only Objects Built From It
aspects.reason: a design trade-off between two structures that behave alike at run time; a graded test can't tell a passed-in factory from an override, and the quiz checks the consequence the page shows, the hook's reach

aspects.says: A creation hook reaches only objects built from the subclass: pools from Executors and the virtual-thread executor never call it, and each new product needs another subclass.
basis: section:Each Product Costs a Subclass, and the Hook Reaches Only Objects Built From It

aspects.says: Whether a factory returns the same object is the factory's decision, and for Integer.valueOf beyond -128 to 127 it is settled at JVM start, so == on a factory's results holds only where its javadoc promises it.
basis: section:new Always Allocates; a Static Factory Can Hand Back an Object It Already Made

aspects.says: A factory's name can say how it reads its arguments where a constructor can't: new BigDecimal(double) takes the exact binary value and BigDecimal.valueOf(double) the value Double.toString prints.
basis: section:A Constructor Can't Say How It Reads Its Arguments; a Factory's Name Can
